answer: An agent economy resists sybil floods by tying each identity to a scarce, slashable reputation stake earned through peer-graded work, not cheap new keys. A fresh wallet starts at a reputation nadir and must submit a sonnet-length reasoning trace per task; honest peers grade it against hidden verdicts, and its pulse rises only when the record is continuous. Clones cannot pool one reputation, since credit never transfers, so the attacker must fund every clone's stake plus the compute to earn a floor score, multiplying cost per identity until the raid is unprofitable.
